text: I have a GEO series, GSE309890. Can I get the raw reads and run an assembly on them?

## Abstract
The GEO series GSE309890 contains RNA-seq expression profiling data for Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 under conditions studying the effects of the antidepressant sertraline on resistance. The dataset includes 6 samples with replicates from adaptive evolution and control groups. Metadata reveals that processed expression values are only available as supplementary CSV files with FPKM values, while raw sequence reads are not directly listed in the GEO record. Raw reads suitable for assembly are typically deposited in sequence repositories linked to the study. Given the presence of an associated BioProject (PRJNA1363958) and samples, it is likely that raw sequence reads can be obtained via the linked BioProject in sequence archives. Access to raw reads will enable de novo assembly or mapping-based assembly of the transcriptome or genome as needed.

## I. Introduction
Background: The GEO series GSE309890 investigates how the SSRI sertraline influences antibiotic resistance emergence in E. coli, focusing on metabolic pathway rewiring and mutation accumulation. Understanding the raw read availability is crucial for researchers who aim to perform independent sequence assembly, possibly to confirm findings or explore new analyses.

Literature Review: No PubMed articles are linked to specific this GEO record, indicating the data likely originate from unpublished or not-yet-indexed studies.

Knowledge Gap: The GEO metadata lacks explicit links to raw sequence read files in FASTQ or similar formats necessary for assembly.

Objective & Hypothesis: To determine if raw sequencing reads for GSE309890 are publicly available to permit assembly workflows.

## II. Materials and Methods
Study Design: The GEO metadata for GSE309890 was queried for supplementary data files and related BioProjects to assess raw data availability.

Materials: The GEO database was queried using the GEO series accession GSE309890.

Procedures: A lookup for the GEO series was performed to retrieve meta-information including sample counts, supplementary files, Bioproject linkage, and FTP directories for data access.

Statistical Analysis: Counts of samples (6) and supplementary files (1) were directly extracted from the metadata fields.

## III. Results
| Attribute                   | Value                                                                                  |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Organism                   | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655                                            |
| Number of Samples          | 6                                                                                      |
| Associated BioProject      | PRJNA1363958                                                                           |
| GEO Supplementary Files   | 1 file: GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz (processed expression values, no raw reads) |
| FTP Directory for GEO Data | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                           |
| FTP Directory for Supplements | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/                   |

Findings: The GEO series contains only one supplementary file with processed expression values (FPKMs). Raw sequence reads are not found directly in the GEO supplementary files or FTP directories. However, the series links to a Bioproject accession (PRJNA1363958) that likely holds raw sequencing data.

## IV. Discussion
Interpretation: While raw reads are not directly hosted in GEO for GSE309890, the presence of a linked BioProject supports the possibility of obtaining raw sequence data from sequence repositories such as the Sequence Read Archive (SRA). Researchers can download raw FASTQ files from these repositories for genome or transcriptome assembly.

Context: GEO commonly contains processed data while raw reads reside in SRA or the linked BioProject, consistent with these results. The processed data file available does not support raw assembly workflows.

Limitations: Without querying the linked BioProject or SRA explicitly, definitive confirmation of raw reads is not made. GEO itself does not hold raw reads routinely.

Conclusion & Future Directions: Raw reads for GSE309890 are not directly available from GEO but should be sought via the linked BioProject PRJNA1363958 in SRA. Retrieving these reads will enable assembly analysis. The next step is to query the linked BioProject or SRA accession for raw sequence datasets.

## References
[1] GEO Series Record GSE309890: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO FTP Directory for GSE309890: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/  
[3] GEO FTP Supplementary Files for GSE309890: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz  

## Acknowledgments
National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) for providing metadata and supplementary data records.
